entries.name: Gray whale (grey whale)
entries.migrates: one of the longest mammal migrations on Earth: summer feeding in the Bering and Okhotsk shelves, winter calving in warm coastal lagoons
behaviour: feeds benthically: rolls onto its right side and sucks up the seabed, leaving feeding pits
blotchy mottled skin encrusted with barnacles and whale lice
famous 16,000-22,000 km round-trip migration; mothers teach the route to calves
recovered from near-extinction after commercial hunting; east Pacific stock bounced back, the Okhotsk stock is still scarce

voxel_model.pattern: mottled grey with orange barnacle patches

entries.notes: The icon of the small frozen shelf seas: grey whales feed in the ice-fringed Bering and Okhotsk flats in summer. gestation_days is roughly 12-13 months. Often seen 'spy-hopping' vertically to look around.

entries.name: Fin whale (finback)
entries.migrates: seasonal: polar shelf feeds in summer, temperate overwintering
behaviour: second largest animal ever to live (only the blue whale is bigger)
the 'greyhound of the sea' - streamlined and fast, up to ~37 km/h
lunges through dense prey shoals with an arched back and their asymmetric jaw
right jaw is white, left is dark - nobody knows quite why

voxel_model.pattern: asymmetric jaw coloration (right white)

entries.notes: Second-heaviest animal on Earth; a classic seasonal visitor to the cold shelves (Newfoundland, Barents, Bering). gestation_days ~11-11.5 months. Vulnerable; still recovering from industrial whaling.

entries.name: Spotted seal (larga seal)
entries.migrates: follows the marginal ice zone; pups are born on drifting pack ice in late winter-spring

breeding.season: late winter-early spring (pups born Feb-Apr on drifting ice)

behaviour: strongly tied to seasonal pack ice - the defining seal of the small frozen shelf seas
dark-ringed 'larga' spots, almost leopard-print
mothers nurse pups for ~3-4 weeks on drifting floes, then molt
very vocal in the breeding season; hauls out in loose groups outside it

voxel_model.pattern: dark spots scattered over silver-grey

entries.notes: The seal of the ice edge in the Bohai, Yellow, Japan, Okhotsk and Bering seas; juveniles are sometimes taken by sea lions. gestation_days includes delayed implantation.

entries.name: Harbor porpoise
behaviour: shy and fast-moving; the 'ghost of the shallows' that never breaches
round head with a short, blunt, spade-shaped beak - nothing like a dolphin's
must eat ~10% of its body weight daily; cannot survive long fasts
Baltic population is critically endangered (~a few hundred left)

voxel_model.pattern: dark dorsal, white belly, blunt beak

entries.notes: The small cetacean people actually see in British, Baltic and New England bays: a rounded head and a barely-seen triangular fin. Bycatch in gillnets is the Baltic population's main threat. gestation_days ~10-11 months.

entries.name: Steller sea lion
entries.migrates: seasonal movements between haulouts, rookeries and foraging grounds
behaviour: largest living eared seal (otariid); males roar like a lion
hauls out on rocky shores and low islands in hundreds or thousands
western stock (Kurils to Gulf of Alaska) crashed ~80% since the 1970s; eastern stock largely recovered
huge sagittal crest and mane; dark chocolate as a bull, tan as a cow

voxel_model.pattern: mane in mature bulls

entries.notes: The barking giant of the Bering and Okhotsk rookeries. gestation_days includes delayed implantation (~1 year total). A great 'rare aggregation' spawn: a cold coast fringed with roaring tan bodies.

entries.name: Northern fur seal
entries.migrates: winters south of the breeding islands along the Pacific rim; summers on the rookeries
behaviour: extreme sexual dimorphism: bulls 30-40% longer and 4.5x heavier than cows
polygynous: a bull holds a harem of up to 50 females and fasts for the whole season
famous 1911 North Pacific Fur Seal Convention - the first international wildlife treaty
rookeries on the Pribilof, Commander and Tyuleniy Islands; vulnerable, Pribilof stock down ~50% since 1970

voxel_model.pattern: creamy underfur glimpsed between dark guard hairs

entries.notes: Males reach 270 kg; females ~50 kg - model both as different mobs. gestation_days is about a year including delayed implantation. The Pribilof haulout of hundreds of thousands is a world-class voxel spectacle.

entries.name: Walleye pollock (Alaska pollock)
entries.migrates: short seasonal shelf migrations; does strong vertical day/night migrations
behaviour: largest single fish stock on Earth - millions of tonnes in the Bering Sea
semi-pelagic schooling fish; the backbone of the Alaska fishery and of McDonald's Filet-O-Fish
shifts north as the Bering Shelf warms; a leading indicator of Arctic change
surimi (fish paste) industry runs almost entirely on pollock

voxel_model.pattern: dark back, pale belly, speckled flanks

entries.notes: Feed the world: the Alaska pollock fishery is the largest certified sustainable fishery on the planet. Without pollock there are no Steller sea lions, fur seals or Rausu Steller's sea eagles.

entries.name: Atlantic herring
entries.migrates: vast trans-shelf migrations between feeding and spawning grounds

breeding.season: any (large spawning runs; main seasons spring and autumn)

behaviour: schools so dense they were mistaken for land by early mariners
silvered flank flashes as a single mass - the 'silver darling' of the North Sea
spawns millions of eggs on coarse gravel; larvae drift in currents
Baltic form 'stromming' is brackish-water and smaller; the Hansa made its fortune on salted herring

voxel_model.pattern: silver sides, blue-black back

entries.notes: The fish that fed medieval Europe: salt + herring built the Hanseatic League. Every predator in the cold shelf ecosystem eats it; collapse the herring and the whole biome starves.

entries.name: Pacific cod (gray cod)
entries.migrates: seasonal; approaches shallow coasts to spawn and feed in winter-spring
behaviour: the Rausu 'winter cod' - thousands of Steller's sea eagles gather on Hokkaido every February for the Pacific cod fishery
bottom-dwelling, aggressive feeder; takes baits at night
slow-growing and long-lived; stocks crash and recover on decade cycles
major commercial fish, sold salted as stockfish-style 'bacalao' in Japan

voxel_model.pattern: mottled brown-grey, chin barbel

entries.notes: The Pacific twin of Atlantic cod; the Rausu February cod fishery is a rare working-town spectacle where eagles and fishers share the catch. Slow-growing - a game currency worth farming, not mining.

entries.name: Capelin
entries.migrates: Barents Sea fish migrate to the coasts to spawn; Icelandic schools cross the ocean
behaviour: beach-spawning: in Newfoundland and Kamchatka they roll onto the sand in millions and people scoop them up
males are semelparous - they spawn and die; post-spawning mortality is near 100% for males
spawn on beaches or sand/gravel at 2-100 m depth; eggs hatch in 5-10 days
the single most important forage fish of the cold shelf; when capelin collapses, cod follow

voxel_model.pattern: olive back, silvery flanks, red iridescence on males

entries.notes: Feeding-frenzy fish: when capelin roll in, gulls, seals, whales and people all feast. Its roe is the 'masago' in sushi. Key forage for cod, puffins and whales.

entries.name: Common murre (common guillemot)
behaviour: nests shoulder-to-shoulder on bare cliff ledges; a single teardrop-shaped egg balanced with no nest
chicks jump from the cliff at 2-3 weeks, guided by the male to the sea
returns to the same few centimetres of ledge, year after year
winters offshore in huge rafting flocks

voxel_model.pattern: dark head and back, white underparts; white facial line

entries.notes: The black-and-white javelin of the cliff face. gestation_days is egg incubation. Pair with thick-billed murre (already in frozen_ocean) to show the Arctic/temperate split along the coast.

entries.name: Great black-backed gull
behaviour: world's largest gull; intimidating aerial predator of other seabirds
will batter a puffin in flight and swallow it whole
raids nests and drops shellfish on rocks to crack them
nests in loose colonies on rocky islets and coastal cliffs

voxel_model.pattern: white head and underparts, black back, pink legs

entries.notes: The apex idiot-bird of cold coasts: too big to ignore, clever enough to steal, and happy at any fish dock. A colony of these should make the beach feel dangerous to nesting birds.

entries.name: White-tailed eagle (sea eagle)
behaviour: massive wingspan (2.0-2.4 m) - can pick a salmon from the shallows or a goose from the air
nests reused for decades; a nest can reach several tonnes of sticks
scavenger-opportunist: steals catch from otters and fishers
recovered from DDT-era collapse across Europe; an icon of reintroduction success

voxel_model.pattern: pale head, wedge-shaped white tail

entries.notes: The great sea eagle of Baltic and North Atlantic coasts; its huge stick nest dominates the coastal silhouette. Close cousin of the bald eagle - where they overlap (Alaska) they hybridise. gestation_days is egg incubation (~5.5 weeks).

entries.name: Snow crab (opilio crab)
entries.migrates: vertical and ontogenetic depth migrations with life stage

breeding.season: spring mating, females brood eggs ~2 years in cold water

behaviour: the source of 'snow crab legs' - the biggest crab fishery in North America
massed on cold shelf sediment; can walk hundreds of km to molt or mate
males fight with a single huge claw; males fished commercially at 9+ cm carapace
2022: the entire Bering Sea fishery was cancelled after the stock crashed ~80% - the first closure in history

voxel_model.pattern: white-spotted brown carapace; length_m measured leg-tip to leg-tip, carapace ~10-13 cm

entries.notes: The poster crab of shelf-sea ice dynamics: warm water pushes the stock out of US waters entirely. A great indicator mob - make it spawn less often as the world warms.

entries.name: Red king crab
entries.migrates: seasonal depth cycles: shallow in winter, deep in summer ('king crab walking')

breeding.season: spring (mating in shallow water; one clutch per year)

behaviour: among the largest crustaceans on Earth; leg span up to 1.8 m
slow, deliberate 'walking' across the shelf; they 'bubble-walk' forward over the sea floor
introduced to the Barents Sea by Soviet scientists in the 1960s - now an invasive giant spreading through Norwegian Finnmark
legendary fishery; pots hauled and walked by fishermen in the same Alaska cold that kills

voxel_model.pattern: spiny dark-red carapace; length_m measured leg-tip to leg-tip, carapace ~20 cm

entries.notes: The crown of the cold shelf: a crab worth more than its weight in silver. In the Barents it is an alien - one red king crab weighs more than a person and walks where it was never supposed to be.

entries.name: Blue mussel
behaviour: cements itself to rock with byssus threads - the 'beard' pulled before cooking
reef-forming filter feeders; they clear a bay's water column in days
brackish Baltic mussels are stunted but sweet; full-salinity North Sea mussels much larger
farmed across Europe for over 700 years; a classic of the mussel pot (moules)

voxel_model.pattern: iridescent blue-black wedges

entries.notes: The unglamorous engine of the cold intertidal: mussel beds feed oystercatchers, eiders, starfish and people. A cheap food source, a water filter, and a reef - three mobs in one.

entries.name: Black guillemot
behaviour: scarlet legs and gape - 'sea hen' in the Old Norse tongue
nests in rock crevices and under boulders, rarely on open ledges
white wing patch flashes in flight; dives and flies with whirring wings
winter visitors in small numbers into the ice-free Baltic and North Sea

voxel_model.pattern: black body, white wing patch, red legs

entries.notes: A jewel of the rocky shore: black suit, white wing flashes, red legs. Nests where other auks cannot - dark crevices under the cliff. gestation_days is egg incubation.

entries.name: Long-tailed duck (oldsquaw)
entries.migrates: Arctic breeding ponds in summer, ice-free Baltic and North Atlantic coasts in winter
behaviour: unmistakable yodelling call 'ow-ow-oo-oo-owdleeo'
male has enormously elongated central tail feathers, swept up in display flight
Baltic Sea is the world's main wintering ground - tens of thousands off Denmark
dives to ~60 m; susceptible to fishing bycatch

voxel_model.pattern: bold black-and-white harlequin; long thin tail streamers on the male

entries.notes: The yodelling duck of the Baltic winter. Vulnerable - bycatch and hunting have driven declines. gestation_days is egg incubation.

entries.name: North Atlantic right whale
entries.migrates: seasonal: Gulf of St Lawrence feeding grounds summer, Georgia/Florida calving grounds winter
behaviour: the 'right' whale - the one whalers called the right to hunt: fat, slow, coastal, floats when dead
no dorsal fin; V-shaped blowhole throws a heart-shaped blow
callosities (barnacle-like white patches) identify individuals like fingerprints
~380 left; only ~70 breeding females; the Gulf of St Lawrence 2017 die-off killed 17 in weeks

voxel_model.pattern: white callosities on head

entries.notes: The rarest large whale in the Atlantic: fewer than 400 remain, ships and fishing gear kill one every few months. Spawning this in a frozen-small-sea biome as a genuinely rare encounter is exactly right. gestation_days ~1 year.

entries.name: Dall's porpoise
behaviour: the bow-riding bullet of cold shelves - regularly clocks 55 km/h
frosted grey flanks with a white belly patch; often mistaken for a baby orca
travels in groups of 2-12 but aggregates of 100+ form over fish schools
deep diver; exploits upwellings full of fish

voxel_model.pattern: black body, white flank frosting and white tail-stock patch

entries.notes: The Pinger in hitch-hiking scenes: Dall's porpoises throw themselves into ship bow waves at full speed. A fun, fast, friendly spawn for the Pacific cold shelf. gestation_days ~11 months.

entries.name: Pacific white-sided dolphin
entries.migrates: follows cold shelf water and fish stocks seasonally
behaviour: acrobat of the cold Pacific - flips and tail-slaps for fun, not just food
stunning backswept dorsal fin with a two-tone 'suspenders' pattern
schools of hundreds or thousands mix with Dall's porpoises over fish shoals
highly social; travels with humpbacks and tuna

voxel_model.pattern: dark cape, light flank, bold black suspender stripes

entries.notes: The 'curvy-fin': unmistakable backswept fin and cheerful gymnastics. The Pacific analog of the Atlantic common dolphin - where shelves freeze in winter, this is your playful dolphin spawn. gestation_days ~12 months.

entries.name: Caspian seal
entries.migrates: summers in the deep south Caspian, winters and breeds on the frozen northern Caspian ice

breeding.season: late autumn-winter (pups born Jan-Feb on northern ice)

behaviour: the landlocked cousin of the ringed seal - isolated since the Arctic link vanished ~2 million years ago
the only seal of the Caspian; pups are born on the northern Caspian's winter ice
monogamous; white 'fairy-tale' pups born on the ice like ringed seals
endangered: population crashed >90% since 1900 to perhaps 50,000-170,000; mass die-offs in 1997-2001 and 2022

voxel_model.pattern: plain grey-brown; pups pure white

entries.notes: The only pinniped in the largest inland sea on Earth - and that sea freezes every winter in the north. A real, living example of 'small frozen ocean' fauna far from any ocean. The 2022 die-off killed 2,500 in weeks; honest rare spawn.

entries.name: Pacific herring
entries.migrates: spawns en masse in shallow eelgrass bays each spring

breeding.season: spring (spawning runs into shallow, sometimes icy bays)

behaviour: spring spawns turn entire bays milky white with 'herring milt'
huge schools roll onto eelgrass beds to deposit eggs in shallow water
keystone prey: this fish feeds ancient harvest cycles of Indigenous peoples and seabird colonies
one of the largest single fisheries in North America; roe (kazunoko) is a New Year delicacy in Japan

voxel_model.pattern: silver sides, blue-green back

entries.notes: Twin of Atlantic herring for the Pacific shelves; the spring 'herring balls' are a feeding frenzy of gulls, eagles, seals and people. Spawning time is the single most dramatic non-whale event in this biome.

entries.name: European sprat
entries.migrates: inshore-offshore seasonal moves between summer feeding and winter shelf water

breeding.season: nearly year-round (main peaks spring and autumn)

behaviour: small flashing schools near the surface
the single most abundant fish in the Baltic - and the only hope for the collapsed Baltic cod
smoked 'Kieler Sprotten' is a German institution
crunched whole as fishmeal; eats and is eaten in equal measure

voxel_model.pattern: slender silver body, blue-green back

entries.notes: The small flashing mass under every Baltic predator: sprat feeds herring, tuna, cod, puffins and terns. Collapse the sprat, and the Baltic cod with it - a good cautionary tale in data form.

entries.name: Sand eel (lesser sand eel)
behaviour: buries itself in the sand at night; feeds in tight shoals by day
the pivotal prey of the North Sea - puffin, murre and razorbill all starve when sandeels fail
UK banned industrial sandeel fishing in 2024 to stop seabird colony collapse
snake-like body; no true swim bladder, so it zizzes just above the seabed

voxel_model.pattern: long, slender, silvery

entries.notes: The invisible keystone: no puffins without sandeels. In a voxel world, a beach strewn with burying eels and hunting puffins is the single clearest 'cold sea' vignette you can build.

entries.name: Greenland halibut (Greenland turbot)
behaviour: deep, cold, slow - the classic rope-fish of the far north
right-eyed flatfish, unlike the left-eyed Atlantic halibut
commercially huge: a major Greenland and Canadian fishery, plus the mysterious 'turbot' scuffles over quotas
slow-growing - a single fishery collapse can last decades

voxel_model.pattern: dark brown-black, blind to light side; off-white belly

entries.notes: The deep-water dividend of the cold shelf. Its fishery ties Greenland, Canada and the US together in shared quotas - a real-world diplomacy mob, not just dinner.

entries.name: Atlantic wolffish (sea cat, wolf-eel)

breeding.season: summer (nests in rock dens; male guards the clutch for ~6-7 months)

behaviour: crushes sea urchins and crabs with molar-like teeth - the jaws of a wolf in a fish
lives in a lair among rocks, emerging at night to hunt
the male guards a football-sized egg mass for months - one of the few fish with devoted fathers
once 'trash fish' tossed overboard; populations crashed ~90% and it is now protected in US and Canadian waters

voxel_model.pattern: banded grey-brown with vertical dark bars

entries.notes: A grumpy monster for the cold rocky den: big head, bulging eyes, a permanent frown. Its near-loss shows how 'bad-tempered trash fish' can still be keystone. Honest, rare, beloved by divers.

entries.name: Lumpfish (lumpsucker)
entries.migrates: spawns in shallow subtidal coasts (Dec-Jun)

breeding.season: winter-spring (shallow nests; male guards the clutch)

behaviour: round, knobbly body with warty tubercles and a suction-disc belly to cling to rocks
famously used as a 'cleaner fish' - farmed lumpfish eat sea lice off farmed salmon
roe harvested as 'lumpfish caviar' - the poor-man's caviar
poor swimmer; mostly benthic on rocky or muddy bottoms

voxel_model.pattern: lumps and warts over olive-brown skin

entries.notes: The grumpy round fish that saved salmon farming: millions are bred to patrol cages picking off sea lice. looks like a toad that fell off a rock and never recovered.

entries.name: Razorbill (razor-billed auk)
entries.migrates: winters offshore at sea; some cross to Newfoundland and Iceland
behaviour: black-and-white, upright, with a tall arched bill crossed by a thin white groove
the last big auk to breed on British shores alongside the guillemot
nests in crevices, under boulders and on cliff ledges; single egg per year
North Sea sandeel crashes hammered razorbill colonies as hard as puffins

voxel_model.pattern: razor-flat black bill with white groove

entries.notes: The cliff partner of the puffin: razorbills nest on the same ledges, the same fishing grounds, the same collapsing sandeel stocks. gestation_days is egg incubation (~5 weeks).

entries.name: Tufted puffin
entries.migrates: spends winters on the open North Pacific
behaviour: the flamboyant cousin of the Atlantic puffin - straw-yellow face plumes and a huge orange bill
burrows on treeless islands; both parents fly fish to the burrow until the puffling fledges
Pribilof and Kuril colonies hold hundreds of thousands on rocky grassland cliffs
spends the winter alone far out at sea

voxel_model.pattern: white face mask, yellow plumes, orange bill

entries.notes: The most magnificent puffin: come ashore in April in tuxedo-yellow and fish until September. gestation_days is egg incubation (~6 weeks).

entries.name: Harlequin duck
entries.migrates: breeds on fast mountain rivers and streams; winters on stormy wave-washed coasts
behaviour: named after the Commedia dell'arte harlequin - slate blue with chestnut sides and white harp-string stripes
winters on the roughest surf coasts, diving into breaking waves
one of the few ducks that keeps strictly to wave-washed rocks in winter
feeds on the spawned salmon eggs and fry in rivers; highly site-faithful

voxel_model.pattern: dark blue with chestnut flanks and white harlequin stripes

entries.notes: The theatre duck of cold surf: white stripes over slate and chestnut. A thinking designer notes it breathes river, not sea - the rare nature of a bird that lives in ice water on both ends of its year. gestation_days ~30 days.

entries.name: Steller's eider
entries.migrates: Arctic breeding ponds in summer, ice-free northern coasts in winter

breeding.season: summer (ground nests on tundra pond shores)

behaviour: smallest of the eiders; males sport an iridescent green head and white neck patch
flocks of dozens to hundreds on the sea ice edge in winter
vulnerable: global population under ~100,000 and falling
nests inland on tundra - the only sea duck that breeds far from the sea

voxel_model.pattern: white head with green patch, black stern (male); brown mottled (female)

entries.notes: The little eider of Yukon-Kuskokwim wisdom: Inuit hunters took them sustainably for generations, then the ducks vanished. A blink-and-miss rare spawn for anyone who knows what they are looking at. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Steller's sea eagle
entries.migrates: Kamchatka and Okhotsk coasts breed in summer, winter on Hokkaido and southern Kurils

breeding.season: spring (giant nests on coast and big rivers)

behaviour: the heaviest eagle on Earth: females 6-9.5 kg, wingspan up to 2.5 m
dark brown with white shoulders, a huge yellow bill, and 14 tail feathers (not 12)
gathers in hundreds on Hokkaido every winter to rob the Rausu Pacific cod fishery
vulnerable: only ~5,000 left, nearly all on Kamchatka and around the Sea of Okhotsk

voxel_model.pattern: black-brown with white shoulders, wedge tail, yellow bill

entries.notes: The rarest eagle anyone in this game should ever meet: white shoulders burning across an Okhotsk morning. The Rausu fishery feeds thousands of them every February - a working town and its eagle mob in one scene.

entries.name: Lion's mane jellyfish

breeding.season: late summer-autumn (planktonic planulae settle in spring)

behaviour: bell up to 2 m across; tentacles reported to 37 m - arguably the longest animal ever recorded
a bloom in the North Sea lights up the whole coast; hundreds may pulse through one bay
sting is painful but rarely worse than nettle-rash; the fringe catches fish like a drift net
the hair mass under the bell is a crowd of hollow, thread-trailing oral arms

voxel_model.pattern: fiery red-orange hair of tentacles trailing behind a amber bell

entries.notes: The monster in the surf: step into a cold bay in late summer and the water itself may sting. Class is listed as mollusc per the catalog's 'other' fallback for cnidarians - a classification honesty note. A jelly that can be taller than a lighthouse is the perfect 'surprising' spawn for a temperate frozen sea.

entries.name: Green sea urchin (northern sea urchin)
behaviour: when sea otters vanish, urchin herds mow the kelp forest down - turning it into a barren 'urchin desert'
herds march across the seabed like slow hedgehog armies
roe (uni) is a delicacy - and the reason urchin fisheries boom and bust
Kelp-forest health is the clearest climate signal in the cold shelf

voxel_model.pattern: globular test beneath green spines

entries.notes: The kelp-keeper of the cold shelf: keep the otters, lose the kelp, lose the fish. A small mob with a very large ecological shadow.

entries.name: Common starfish (sugar star)
behaviour: pries mussels open with tube feet, then everts its stomach into the shell to digest the living animal
holds a mussel for hours - a classic rockpool duel
plagues descend on mussel beds in early summer
almost nothing eats it: it tastes foul and is mildly toxic

voxel_model.pattern: orange-red, five arms, white spines on the upper side

entries.notes: The quiet engine of the mussel bed: everted stomach, hours of patient leverage. A common, beautiful, untouchable animal of cold rock pools - perfect ambient life for a frozen coast.
